title: The devotee who is dear to Krishna

verses.sa: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
verses.tr: The one who disturbs no one and is disturbed by no one, and who is free from delight, envy, fear, and agitation, is dear to me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna names four inner enemies a devotee must drop. Listen for the word that means to agitate or unsettle.

body.text: The one who disturbs no one and is disturbed by no one, and who is free from delight, envy, fear, and agitation, is dear to me. The word udvijate means to agitate. Krishna says a devotee is free from both giving agitation and receiving it, and is also free from delight, resentment, envy, and fear. Krishna then adds that a devotee has no expectation, is pure, and has given up all undertakings.

verses.sa: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
verses.tr: One who has no expectation, is pure, skilled, detached, free from anxiety, and has given up all undertakings is dear to me, my devotee.
verses.angle: Anapeksha, without expectation, leads the list
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his description of the devotee who is close to him. Listen for the quality that removes the urge to start anything new.

body.text: One who has no expectation, is pure, skilled, detached, free from anxiety, and has given up all undertakings is dear to me, my devotee. The first word here is anapeksha, without expectation. It heads a list of a person who is pure, skilled, detached, and free from distress, and it reveals that the beloved devotee has no restless urge to launch new undertakings. Krishna then adds that the beloved one is free from attachment to both good and bad actions.

verses.sa: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्ितमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥
verses.tr: One who neither rejoices, hates, grieves, nor craves, and who has given up attachment to both good and bad actions, is dear to me.
verses.angle: Bhakti: the mark of the devoted
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues to describe the devotee who has given up clinging to both good and bad actions. Listen for the exact list of what this person no longer does.

body.text: One who neither rejoices, hates, grieves, nor craves, and who has given up attachment to both good and bad actions, is dear to me. The word bhakti, devotion, is named here as the mark of the person who has let go of both good and bad actions. Krishna now lists more pairs the devotee faces without reaction, starting with enemy and friend.

verses.sa: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥
verses.tr: One who is equal to enemy and friend, honor and dishonor, heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and is free from attachment is dear to Me.
verses.angle: samah: the steady state of being equal
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: What does it take to remain steady when the world pushes and pulls on every side? Krishna names the pairs that usually throw a person off balance.

body.text: One who is equal to enemy and friend, honor and dishonor, heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and is free from attachment is dear to Me. The Sanskrit word samah, equal, appears twice in this verse. It marks the steady state Krishna asks of a devotee, someone who does not tilt toward friend or enemy, or toward comfort or pain. Krishna now names the outer signs of that steadiness in the next verse.

verses.sa: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्ितमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
verses.tr: Equal in praise and blame, silent, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady-minded, the devoted person is dear to me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes the inner life of a steady devotee. Listen for the details he adds to this portrait.

body.text: Equal in praise and blame, silent, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady-minded, the devoted person is dear to me. Krishna adds praise and blame to the list, and then silence, and then having no fixed home, aniketah. The devotee is steady-minded because he has stopped clinging to a place, a body, or to opinions. Krishna then turns to the devotees who trust him and live this nectar-like teaching.

verses.sa: ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते । श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥
verses.tr: Those devotees who trust, take refuge in Me, and faithfully live this nectar-like teaching are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is closing chapter 12 by naming the exact action that makes a devotee dear to him. Listen for the word that means to practice.

body.text: Those devotees who trust, take refuge in Me, and faithfully live this nectar-like teaching are exceedingly dear to Me. The word is paryupasate, to diligently practice. It is not enough to trust or to hold Krishna as the highest aim; the devotee must actively live this nectar-like teaching, and that practice is what makes them exceedingly dear to him. Arjuna now asks to understand the teaching itself, beginning with the nature of the field and the knower of the field.
